title: RedCap architecture smell governance backlog
purpose: Capture the architecture, knowledge, evidence, runtime, and productization smells found during the post-P4-2k global review so later work can close them deliberately instead of rediscovering them from chat context.
source_context: The non-release pre-publication productization task is closed, but the user asked for a senior AI Agent engineering review beyond task-completion bookkeeping.
The directory/knowledge-layer concern is treated as an example, not as the whole problem space.

This backlog intentionally separates active commitments from improvement candidates. Items here are not automatically completed work and must be opened as implementation slices before being claimed done.

priority_semantics.P0: Should be handled before any serious public release readiness claim because it affects retrieval correctness, truth-source clarity, or future task reliability.
priority_semantics.P1: High-value productization or architecture debt; safe to schedule after P0, but should not be allowed to drift indefinitely.
priority_semantics.P2: Important governance hardening; not blocking current local usage, but prevents future entropy.
priority_semantics.P3: Longer-horizon capability or scale work; keep visible and threshold-triggered.

tranches.title: Fast consistency and truth-surface repairs
tranches.intent: Fix low-cost drift that misleads humans or agents even when runtime checks pass.

tranches.title: Knowledge architecture foundations
tranches.intent: Turn the current multi-root knowledge layout into a deliberate federated retrieval system instead of a loose pile of knowledge directories.

tranches.title: Policy, evidence, and legacy-asset hygiene
tranches.intent: Reduce policy sprawl, evidence accumulation, and old/new transition ambiguity without damaging archaeology.

tranches.title: Runtime and host-adapter productization
tranches.intent: Move from skill-root compatibility to a cleaner installable runtime and host-adapter shape.

tranches.title: Advanced memory and shared arsenal evolution
tranches.intent: Keep full LLM-wiki, retrieval escalation, and public arsenal maturity visible without prematurely enabling heavyweight memory systems.

tranches.title: Root product-shape consolidation
tranches.intent: Judge whether the repository root itself still exposes too many direct parent directories for knowledge, reports, evidence, runtime, and public templates before RedCap is treated as a clean product.

tranches.title: Senior holistic smell audit
tranches.intent: Prevent user examples from being narrowed into single-point fixes by requiring a Prism-reviewed, senior-engineering review across RedCap's product shape, workflow guarantees, truth sources, knowledge/evidence lifecycle, package surface, and human-facing status model.

tranches.title: Holistic audit follow-up before release readiness
tranches.intent: Track the P1 issues discovered by RASG-018 that should be closed before RedCap is treated as a polished public runtime or CLI product.

tranches.title: Plan-only closure and Prism follow-up hardening
tranches.intent: Prevent design-only, plan-only, or route-only work from being treated as fully closed when a later physical apply or governance hardening task was explicitly required.

requirements.title: Split the giant lessons.md into indexed topic modules
requirements.problem_source: compass/knowledge/lessons.md is an active private knowledge file of about 198KB, making it a single-file retrieval and token-pressure hotspot.
requirements.risk: Index-first rules mitigate bulk-loading, but the physical single-file shape still degrades grep precision, makes exact slicing hard, and will get worse as lessons grow.
requirements.desired_outcome: Lessons become a topic-indexed, small-file knowledge set with stable IDs, source anchors, and a human-readable index. No lesson should be lost or silently rewritten.
implementation_notes: Design a reversible split plan before moving content.
Keep old L-number anchors resolvable through an alias map.
Update knowledge index, token-risk audit, and any lesson lookup checks.
acceptance: No default import reads the old monolith.
Existing lesson references still resolve.
Knowledge index check and token-risk audit pass.

requirements.title: Create a federated knowledge lookup route across active knowledge, LLM-wiki-lite, cold archive, and public arsenal
requirements.problem_source: RedCap currently has compass/knowledge, redcap-knowledge, shared-knowledge, and external redcap-arsenal with defined roles but no single user-facing lookup route.
requirements.risk: Agents may either miss relevant cold/public knowledge or over-scan multiple roots, recreating the token and context-pollution problem through a different path.
requirements.desired_outcome: A single knowledge gateway policy and command explain where to search first, when to fall back, and when exact-body reads are allowed.
implementation_notes: Define route order: active index, LLM-wiki-lite metadata, public arsenal catalog, cold archive catalog, exact evidence.
Make cold archive fallback explicit and measurable.
Keep source files authoritative; derived summaries must not replace truth sources.
acceptance: A user or agent can answer where to look for each knowledge class without reading multiple README files.
Spec/diagnose can validate the route policy.
The route prevents default full-corpus loading.

requirements.title: Fix shared-knowledge template README drift against external redcap-arsenal state
requirements.problem_source: shared-knowledge/README.md still says template-only while the external redcap-arsenal worktree already contains Forge-reviewed substantive entries.
requirements.risk: Humans or agents may treat shared-knowledge as the real public repository state and make wrong write/read decisions.
requirements.desired_outcome: The template README clearly distinguishes the template source from the external arsenal worktree and states that the external worktree may contain reviewed entries.
implementation_notes: Do not move public entries back into shared-knowledge.
Reference shared-knowledge-remote-binding as the state source for external worktree status.
Keep claims conservative: first reviewed sample set, not mature public knowledge base.
acceptance: No template-only wording contradicts reviewed-substantive external state.
Public-arsenal claim boundary check still passes.

requirements.title: Triage redcap-knowledge cold archive into preserve, translate, or prune classes
requirements.problem_source: redcap-knowledge contains about 69 files and nearly 1MB of private cold archive content, larger than the active knowledge layer.
requirements.risk: Cold archive may hide valuable reusable knowledge, stale private reports, or dead evidence. Without triage, the archive becomes a silent maintenance burden.
requirements.desired_outcome: Each cold archive asset has a lifecycle class: preserve for archaeology, translate into active/public knowledge through Forge, or prune when safe.
implementation_notes: Start with inventory and metadata; do not bulk-read everything into the main context.
Preserve evidence needed by receipts, reports, and architecture traces.
Use RedCap Forge for any public distillation.
acceptance: Cold archive inventory is machine-readable.
No raw private archive is exported to public arsenal.
Prune candidates are dry-run reviewed before apply.

requirements.title: De-sprawl references into authority policy, active configuration, and historical migration evidence
requirements.problem_source: references has 66 files and more than 1MB of mixed policy, migration manifests, one-off plans, and long-lived control truth.
requirements.risk: A directory named references becomes a policy junk drawer; future agents cannot tell which files are executable authority and which are historical evidence.
requirements.desired_outcome: References have explicit classes and retrieval routes; one-off migration evidence is not confused with active policy.
implementation_notes: Do not physically move high-risk files before alias and consumer checks exist.
Prefer catalog/classification first, then migration in small reversible slices.
Keep file lookup dictionary in sync.
acceptance: Each large reference file has a class and lifecycle.
Spec-check and file lookup dictionary checks pass.
No active policy loses its consumer.

requirements.title: Complete or explicitly block full runtime physical split before public release
requirements.problem_source: runtime/ currently provides package-visible wrappers and an import map, while authoritative tools still live under root compass/prism paths.
requirements.risk: Publishing this shape as a public runtime may freeze compatibility wrappers as public API and make later physical split a breaking change.
requirements.desired_outcome: Either complete a real runtime-core split, or make the wrapper-based shape an explicit alpha contract with clear non-stability boundaries.
implementation_notes: Do not move tool trees in a single large patch.
First map runtime-required tools, host adapters, and source-maintainer-only tools.
Keep clean workspace E2E and package publish safety in the loop.
acceptance: Release readiness can explain whether runtime is physically split or intentionally alpha-wrapper-based.
No hidden dependency on Norven's local skill-root path remains in packaged commands.

requirements.title: Make package surface include/exclude rules single-source generated
requirements.problem_source: package.json files and runtime/package safety policies are currently checked for drift, but the include/exclude list still exists in multiple places.
requirements.risk: Manual duplication can drift silently between package.json, runtime package policy, and publish-safety policy before a future release.
requirements.desired_outcome: One machine-readable source generates or validates all package include/exclude surfaces.
implementation_notes: Resolve the current special-case difference where package.json omits package.json implicitly and excludes prism/README.md while policy candidates mention it.
Fail closed if generated and checked surfaces differ.
acceptance: Package manifest, public package surface, and publish safety read from the same source or prove exact equivalence.
npm pack dry-run still passes.

requirements.title: Add stronger prism/runs evidence rotation, compression, and lookup policy
requirements.problem_source: prism/runs contains about 599 files and 8.5MB of raw run evidence, with only one currently pruneable local-evidence directory.
requirements.risk: Gitignore prevents repo bloat, but local evidence can still become unreadable and expensive to scan.
requirements.desired_outcome: Formal evidence remains replayable while raw bulky output is timeboxed, compressed, or summarized through indexes.
implementation_notes: Preserve referenced formal runs by default.
Compress or prune only after lifecycle classification.
Expose a human-readable inventory summary.
acceptance: prism-runs-lifecycle can report, dry-run, and safely apply approved cleanup.
No bound evidence referenced by reports is deleted.

requirements.title: Improve closeout final-state observability when earlier retries failed
requirements.problem_source: A previous on-complete retry failure can remain in audit logs even when a later receipt successfully closes the task.
requirements.risk: External reviewers may see a failed audit and misread it as the final task state.
requirements.desired_outcome: Status surfaces clearly show final state, previous failed attempts, and the successful repair/closure sequence.
implementation_notes: Do not hide failed attempts.
Group attempts under a final-state timeline.
Make current-status and closeout status agree on the final outcome.
acceptance: A user can tell at a glance that the task is completed despite earlier failed attempts.
Failed attempts remain auditable.

requirements.title: Promote full LLM-wiki from sleeping future item to a thresholded active roadmap
requirements.problem_source: LLM-wiki-lite exists with a private non-authoritative entry, while full LLM-wiki, background distillation, FTS/RAG/GraphRAG remain future thresholded capabilities.
requirements.risk: The capability is not lost in machine files, but it can become invisible in day-to-day planning and never get activated when conditions are met.
requirements.desired_outcome: Full LLM-wiki has explicit activation criteria, owner gates, non-goals, and a first implementation tranche that does not prematurely enable heavy RAG.
implementation_notes: Keep LLM-wiki non-authoritative and source-anchored.
Separate full LLM-wiki product work from RAG/GraphRAG backend escalation.
Avoid turning semantic summaries into truth sources.
acceptance: Roadmap status is visible in current-status or backlog views.
Threshold crossing opens a task instead of silently enabling heavy retrieval.
LLM-wiki-lite checks continue to pass.

requirements.title: Enforce retrieval observation metrics for FTS, RAG, and GraphRAG escalation
requirements.problem_source: retrieval-escalation-policy defines thresholds, but observation metrics depend on future reports recording retrieval misses.
requirements.risk: Thresholded architecture can degrade into subjective judgment if misses are not consistently recorded.
requirements.desired_outcome: Real retrieval misses and noisy lookup events are recorded in a structured place and checked before route escalation.
implementation_notes: Add lightweight observation logging to task reports or current-status-compatible policy state.
Do not count guesses as misses.
Keep RAG/GraphRAG opt-in until thresholds and Prism review pass.
acceptance: A task that reports retrieval failure updates observation metrics or explains why not.
retrieval-escalation-check enforces the rule.

requirements.title: Unify host-adapter entry generation and avoid copied rule drift
requirements.problem_source: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, and runtime host adapters coexist with root-level host directories.
requirements.risk: Host-specific entry files can drift, and future adapters may duplicate RedCap authority rules instead of pointing to the same source.
requirements.desired_outcome: Host adapters are generated or verified from a single source and remain thin entry points.
implementation_notes: Do not assume all hosts support the same hook strength.
Keep host capability matrix explicit.
Preserve Codex.app host-limited boundaries.
acceptance: Adapter drift is machine-detectable.
Host entries do not duplicate long rule bodies.

requirements.title: Review Layer A loom legacy assets against modern Layer B and Prism architecture
requirements.problem_source: loom still contains Layer A dispatcher roles, adapters, and reports while Layer B now uses a different FSM/receipt/Prism control model.
requirements.risk: Old Dispatcher concepts can confuse RedCap self-development semantics and make new contributors believe Layer A and Layer B share the same runtime entry.
requirements.desired_outcome: Layer A assets are either clearly retained for external user-project workflows, migrated, or archived with compatibility notes.
implementation_notes: Do not delete Layer A simply because Layer B is newer.
Document the distinction in a human-readable system map.
Check references before moving anything.
acceptance: Layer A vs Layer B ownership is obvious from file lookup and README surfaces.
No Layer A command used by acceptance tests breaks.

requirements.title: Automate active task-report rotation from compass/docs to private archive
requirements.problem_source: compass/docs/task-reports is capped by policy, but reports still accumulate in the active docs inbox until lifecycle work moves them.
requirements.risk: The active docs area can become a date-sorted report pile and confuse current docs with historical evidence.
requirements.desired_outcome: Recent reports stay visible; older reports move to redcap-knowledge with catalog and alias preservation.
implementation_notes: Use dry-run first.
Keep docs catalog and links valid.
Do not break receipt report_path references.
acceptance: Active report count remains within policy.
Archived reports remain discoverable by catalog/alias.

requirements.title: Define version coupling between RedCap runtime and external redcap-arsenal
requirements.problem_source: The external redcap-arsenal repo is separate from RedCap runtime but can contain entries referenced by RedCap reports, policies, or future skills.
requirements.risk: A runtime version may depend on knowledge entries whose external state has moved, making reproducibility unclear.
requirements.desired_outcome: RedCap records which arsenal commit/head was validated and how runtime releases reference compatible arsenal states.
implementation_notes: Do not force redcap-arsenal into the RedCap repo.
Use remote binding last_verified and optional tags or manifest pins.
Keep append-only public entry rules.
acceptance: A release-readiness check can report the validated arsenal head.
Arsenal drift is visible and fail-closed when required.

requirements.title: Expand clean workspace E2E from same-machine clone to release-grade environment matrix
requirements.problem_source: Clean workspace E2E passes locally, but broader release confidence requires different host and environment assumptions.
requirements.risk: A package can pass on Norven's machine while still failing for a fresh user, a different shell, or a different OS.
requirements.desired_outcome: Release readiness can distinguish local clean clone confidence from multi-environment product confidence.
implementation_notes: Keep this out of non-release task claims.
Start with documented matrix design before automation.
Do not require public npm publish for dry-run testing.
acceptance: Release handoff lists the current environment coverage.
Future release task has a clear test matrix.

requirements.title: Consolidate root-level information architecture before product release
requirements.problem_source: RedCap still exposes multiple direct root children that carry overlapping docs, knowledge, report, archive, evidence, public-template, and control-plane meanings: compass/docs, compass/knowledge, redcap-knowledge, shared-knowledge, prism/reports, prism/runs, loom/test-reports, references, runtime, and related host/runtime roots. Previous RASG work made these roots indexed, safer, and release-filtered, but did not judge or consolidate the root-level parent model itself.
requirements.risk: A future public runtime or contributor-facing repository may freeze the current root shape as product surface. Even if token and package leakage are controlled, humans and agents still pay cognitive cost when related knowledge/report/evidence assets live under several top-level parents with similar meanings.
requirements.desired_outcome: Produce a Prism-reviewed root-level information architecture consolidation plan that inventories every root-level asset root, classifies it, defines a target parent model, maps aliases and consumers, and only then opens any physical migration task.
implementation_notes: Do not immediately move or delete directories in the intake task.
Separate design debt registration from later physical apply.
Classify roots at least as runtime, control-plane, private-archive, public-template, evidence, legacy, host-config, or external-worktree pointer.

Identify consumers before migration: scripts, checks, package files list, host adapters, AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI/Copilot entry files, revive/install/closeout, docs catalog, knowledge gateway, receipt paths, and Prism run evidence.
Require alias, import-map, or compatibility strategy before any path move.
Keep archaeology and receipt anchors discoverable after any future apply.
acceptance: A machine-readable root asset inventory exists and classifies each direct root child that carries RedCap product/runtime/knowledge/evidence meaning.
A target parent model exists and explains which root-level parents should remain, merge, move under an internal root, move outside the repo, or stay as compatibility shims.
A consumer-impact matrix identifies affected scripts, policies, package manifests, host adapters, entry docs, receipt/report anchors, and ignored runtime evidence before any physical migration.
Any future apply task has a dry-run, rollback plan, alias/compatibility window, Prism review, clean-workspace E2E, package-safety check, and closeout receipt.
The progress meter shows this item as open historical debt until the planning and any approved apply tasks are separately receipted.

requirements.title: Run a senior holistic RedCap architecture smell audit instead of closing user examples one by one
requirements.problem_source: The root-level directory concern was originally meant as an example that should trigger a broader senior-engineering review. The intake for RASG-017 correctly registered the concrete root information-architecture debt, but it did not separately register the wider '举一反三' obligation to inspect RedCap for other expert-level smells beyond that single example.
requirements.risk: If every user example is handled as an isolated requirement, RedCap can repeatedly claim local closure while leaving adjacent design smells undiscovered: truth-source ambiguity, old/new transition residue, duplicate control planes, weak human status surfaces, package/runtime boundary leakage, evidence/report lifecycle drift, Prism governance gaps, or token/retrieval hotspots outside the originally named directory.
requirements.desired_outcome: Produce a Prism-reviewed senior holistic architecture smell audit that explicitly reviews multiple domains, records 'found / not found / deferred' conclusions per domain, and gives every finding a durable disposition instead of relying on chat memory. Newly found P0/P1 bad smells must become tracked requirements; lower-priority findings must at least enter a candidate, archive, or deferred register with evidence and revisit criteria.
implementation_notes: Treat RASG-017 as one concrete child concern; do not let it satisfy the broader holistic audit obligation.
The audit must use at least two independent Prism reviewers when available, with Copilot protected as fallback according to provider policy.

Review domains must include root/product shape, active vs cold knowledge, public vs private assets, reports and receipts, Prism evidence, workflow/FSM guarantees, host adapters/hooks, package/release surface, human-facing status/report quality, token/retrieval pressure, and old/new transition residue.
For each domain, require a short human-readable conclusion and a machine-readable finding row; 'no issue found' must be explicit, not silent.

Every finding, including P2/P3 and informational observations, must have an explicit disposition: backlog requirement, linked existing requirement, candidate pool, archive-only note, or deferred item with reason, owner surface, and revisit criteria.
Any P0/P1 finding must either become a backlog requirement or be explicitly deferred with reason, owner surface, acceptance boundary, and Prism-reviewed justification.
The audit must not physically move/delete assets; it is a discovery and task-tree hardening step.
acceptance: A machine-readable holistic smell audit artifact exists and lists every reviewed domain with status, evidence, and follow-up disposition.
A human-readable report explains what was reviewed, what was found, what was not found, and what remains deferred without relying on internal jargon as the main narrative.
At least two Prism reviewers pass the audit plan or result, or a resource-limited acceptance record explains why quorum was unavailable.
Every newly discovered P0/P1 smell is either added to this backlog or explicitly linked to an existing requirement with no duplicate truth source.
Every lower-priority finding has a recorded disposition and cannot be silently discarded from the audit output.
The final closeout explicitly states that RASG-018 is not satisfied by RASG-017 alone.

requirements.title: Make human-facing CLI, status, and notification output understandable without RedCap internal jargon
requirements.problem_source: RASG-018 Prism review found that user-facing surfaces still expose internal terms such as Layer B, Prism quorum, FSM, closeout runtime, receipt, diagnose, and internal gate names as the main narrative.
requirements.risk: A new user can see that RedCap did something but cannot tell what was solved, what remains, whether human help is needed, or where the current work sits in the larger task picture. This turns governance detail into product noise.
requirements.desired_outcome: Human-facing output is framed by problem, action, result, current task panorama, next step, and whether human intervention is needed. Internal mechanism names may appear only as secondary evidence links or glossary-backed details.
implementation_notes: Audit bin/redcap help/status/diagnose output, closeout summaries, Feishu node reports, progress-meter summaries, and task-report executive summaries.
Keep machine-readable evidence intact; this is a presentation-layer cleanup, not a reduction of governance rigor.
Use the existing glossary/file lookup dictionary only as supporting evidence, not as the primary explanation.
acceptance: A first-time human can understand the current task state and next action without knowing RedCap internal component names.
Feishu and CLI summaries include a broad task panorama when the task is part of a larger parent line.
Mechanism names are either avoided in the main narrative or accompanied by a concise human explanation.

requirements.title: Separate public runtime contract from maintainer-only governance validators before npm or CLI release
requirements.problem_source: RASG-018 Prism review found that the current npm candidate surface still exposes a broad mix of runtime entry points, governance validators, Prism tooling, package checks, and maintainer control-plane scripts.
requirements.risk: If published as-is, internal validation tools can be mistaken for stable public API, future cleanup becomes a compatibility problem, and users are forced to understand maintainer-only machinery before using RedCap as a normal tool.
requirements.desired_outcome: Release readiness distinguishes the public runtime contract from maintainer/developer governance tools. The package manifest, runtime package readiness policy, and publish safety check agree on that boundary from a single source or a proved-equivalent source set.
implementation_notes: Do not publish or remove safety checks while this remains planned.
Classify package candidates as runtime-contract, host-adapter, documentation, maintainer-only, private-local, or excluded.
If the first release intentionally includes maintainer tools, make that an explicit alpha contract rather than an accidental public surface.
acceptance: Release readiness can explain which commands are public user contract and which are maintainer/internal contract.
npm pack dry-run remains safe and does not include private files, secrets, volatile evidence, or Norven-local state.
Public package documentation does not present maintainer-only validators as normal end-user workflow.

requirements.title: Track Prism degradation frequency and keep conclusion gates resilient when providers are flaky
requirements.human_label: RASG-021 棱镜降级频率与结论韧性跟踪
requirements.problem_source: RASG-018 Prism review found multiple recent formal Prism runs recorded as resource-limited-pass, mostly because one provider timed out, hit quota, or returned unusable output.
requirements.risk: If resource-limited outcomes become normal, RedCap can slowly drift from multi-view review back to single-agent conclusion making while still sounding Prism-backed.
requirements.desired_outcome: Prism status surfaces show the recent degradation rate, provider families involved, and whether the current task used full quorum or resource-limited evidence. Degradation above a defined threshold opens a governance action instead of being buried in reports.
implementation_notes: Use existing prism/reports/index.yaml and session registries as the first data source; do not bulk-read raw prism/runs by default.
Keep Copilot protected fallback and Codex last-resort policy intact.
Consider a later P2 synthesis-faithfulness machine gate, but do not conflate it with the degradation-frequency P1 unless implementation scope remains small.
acceptance: diagnose or an equivalent status surface reports Prism full-quorum versus resource-limited frequency over a recent window.
A threshold breach creates a visible action or warning instead of silently passing as normal.
Acceptance reports clearly distinguish full Prism quorum from honest resource-limited evidence.

requirements.title: Apply root-level information architecture physical consolidation through safe semantic tranches
requirements.human_label: RASG-022 根目录信息架构的真实物理合并
requirements.problem_source: RASG-017 produced the root-level target model and explicitly set physical_migration_applied=false, but no open backlog item represented the required later physical apply. That made the directory-structure debt easy to lose from the live task rhythm.
requirements.risk: Humans and agents can see RASG-017 as done and assume scattered docs, knowledge, report, evidence, runtime, and template roots were actually consolidated. This recreates the exact reliance on human memory that RedCap is supposed to reduce.
requirements.desired_outcome: Execute or explicitly defer the approved root information architecture physical consolidation in small semantic apply tranches. Each tranche must preserve aliases, consumers, package safety, archaeology anchors, rollback paths, Prism review, clean-workspace E2E, and closeout receipt before any directory move is claimed complete.
implementation_notes: Start from references/root-information-architecture-consolidation-plan.json; do not redesign the target model from chat memory.
Apply at most one semantic parent group per task, with dry-run manifest before any real move.
Keep host entries, package root controls, private local state, and ignored runtime evidence under their documented no-move boundaries unless a separate approval changes the product philosophy.
Update file lookup dictionary, docs catalog, package surface checks, runtime import maps, host adapters, receipt/report anchors, and legacy alias routes in the same tranche as any physical move.
If physical consolidation is still not safe before release readiness, record an explicit blocked/deferred receipt instead of letting this item disappear.
acceptance: A separate apply task card or approved deferral receipt exists before RASG-022 can be closed.
Every physical move has a dry-run manifest, exact consumer matrix, alias/compatibility window, rollback plan, package-safety proof, clean-workspace E2E, and Prism review.
Current status and progress-meter surfaces show whether root physical consolidation is done, deferred, or still open; plan-only completion cannot satisfy this item.
No report claims scattered root information architecture was physically consolidated unless the apply receipt proves it.
requirements.progress_note: shared-knowledge template root and private archive root have applied tranches; remaining high-risk root groups are still explicitly deferred before release readiness.

applied_tranches.completion_boundary: This tranche does not close all root information architecture physical consolidation.
This tranche does not close all root information architecture physical consolidation.

explicit_deferrals.completion_boundary: This keeps the remaining high-risk roots deferred; shared-knowledge and private-archive have applied tranches.

requirements.title: Strengthen Prism and conclusion gates to catch plan-only closure follow-up gaps
requirements.human_label: RASG-023 计划型完成必须登记后续任务的棱镜加固
requirements.problem_source: RASG-017 reviewers correctly accepted the target model as a design artifact, but the workflow did not force the explicitly required physical apply follow-up to become an open backlog item. The gap was exposed by Norven's manual memory challenge rather than by RedCap itself.
requirements.risk: Future plan-only, route-only, or partial-with-defer tasks can pass review while their deferred work remains only inside prose. That creates a false completed state and makes Prism look stronger than the orchestration contract actually is.
requirements.desired_outcome: Prism prompts, conclusion policy, and closeout-facing validators require reviewers to check whether every deferred capability or future apply requirement has a durable task, backlog item, owner surface, or explicit no-follow-up justification before a completion or roadmap verdict is accepted.
implementation_notes: Treat this as an orchestration and prompt/checker defect, not as a single provider quality defect.
Add a closure-gap question to Prism framing for completion, roadmap, architecture, and governance reviews: what is intentionally not done, and where is that follow-up tracked?
Make plan-only completion claims fail closed unless the deferred apply item is linked to a task tree, backlog requirement, receipt, or explicit deferral record.
Use RASG-017/RASG-022 as a regression fixture for the new rule.
acceptance: Prism/conclusion policy explicitly distinguishes design-complete from physically applied completion.
A validator or review checklist can reject a plan-only completion claim when required follow-up tasks are not registered.
RASG-017 remains linked to RASG-022 as its physical apply follow-up, and status surfaces do not imply physical consolidation is complete.
Future official completion or roadmap conclusions must report deferred work, durable follow-up tracking, and a revisit trigger or deadline.

must_not_claim: Do not claim these requirements are completed merely because they are listed here.
Do not claim RASG-001..016 solved root-level physical product-shape consolidation; they solved indexing, lifecycle, retrieval, package safety, and specific root-local policies.
Do not claim RASG-017 physically consolidated root directories; it completed the target model and required RASG-022 for apply or explicit deferral.
Do not claim the user's '举一反三' request has been satisfied by registering only RASG-017; RASG-018 must complete a separate senior holistic audit.
Do not claim RASG-018 fixes the P1 issues it discovered; RASG-019, RASG-020, RASG-021, RASG-022, and RASG-023 each required separate follow-up work with independent receipts.
Do not treat future full LLM-wiki/RAG/GraphRAG as enabled by this backlog.
Do not move or delete historical evidence without dry-run, alias, and receipt-safety checks.
Do not start npm publish from this backlog; release remains a separate task.
recommended_next_step: Before formal npm/public release readiness, run the release-readiness task tree deliberately. RASG-022 is closed for the current pass by one safe physical tranche plus explicit deferral of high-risk root moves; do not claim all high-risk roots were physically moved.

authority_boundary.backlog_responsibility: Machine-readable source for RASG debt items, status, priority, evidence and current focus.
authority_boundary.dev_task_responsibility: Current execution slice, promises, closeout report and active-slice boundary.
authority_boundary.human_guide_responsibility: Human-readable status explanation generated from the backlog authority; it must not override machine truth.

required_headings: ## 当前状态总览（自动同步）

glossary.label: Architecture smell governance item
glossary.meaning: RedCap 架构坏味治理条目，用来记录仍会影响工程健康、发布准备或长期演进的设计债务。

glossary.label: Small safe implementation slice
glossary.meaning: 一次只处理一个可验证的小切片，避免大规模重构同时破坏多个真相源。

glossary.label: Active debt item
glossary.meaning: 当前正在执行或刚完成收口的 backlog 项，必须和 .dev-task.md 的 backlog_item 对齐。

items.title: Fix shared-knowledge template README drift against external redcap-arsenal state
items.summary: The template README clearly distinguishes the template source from the external arsenal worktree and states that the external worktree may contain reviewed entries.

items.title: Make package surface include/exclude rules single-source generated
items.summary: One machine-readable source generates or validates all package include/exclude surfaces.

items.title: Improve closeout final-state observability when earlier retries failed
items.summary: Status surfaces clearly show final state, previous failed attempts, and the successful repair/closure sequence.

items.title: Split the giant lessons.md into indexed topic modules
items.summary: Lessons become a topic-indexed, small-file knowledge set with stable IDs, source anchors, and a human-readable index. No lesson should be lost or silently rewritten.

items.title: Create a federated knowledge lookup route across active knowledge, LLM-wiki-lite, cold archive, and public arsenal
items.summary: A single knowledge gateway policy and command explain where to search first, when to fall back, and when exact-body reads are allowed.

items.title: Triage redcap-knowledge cold archive into preserve, translate, or prune classes
items.summary: Each cold archive asset has a lifecycle class: preserve for archaeology, translate into active/public knowledge through Forge, or prune when safe.

items.title: Automate active task-report rotation from compass/docs to private archive
items.summary: Recent reports stay visible; older reports move to redcap-knowledge with catalog and alias preservation.

items.title: De-sprawl references into authority policy, active configuration, and historical migration evidence
items.summary: References have explicit classes and retrieval routes; one-off migration evidence is not confused with active policy.

items.title: Add stronger prism/runs evidence rotation, compression, and lookup policy
items.summary: Formal evidence remains replayable while raw bulky output is timeboxed, compressed, or summarized through indexes.

items.title: Review Layer A loom legacy assets against modern Layer B and Prism architecture
items.summary: Layer A assets are either clearly retained for external user-project workflows, migrated, or archived with compatibility notes.

items.title: Complete or explicitly block full runtime physical split before public release
items.summary: Either complete a real runtime-core split, or make the wrapper-based shape an explicit alpha contract with clear non-stability boundaries.

items.title: Unify host-adapter entry generation and avoid copied rule drift
items.summary: Host adapters are generated or verified from a single source and remain thin entry points.

items.title: Expand clean workspace E2E from same-machine clone to release-grade environment matrix
items.summary: Release readiness can distinguish local clean clone confidence from multi-environment product confidence.

groups.title: Advanced memory and shared arsenal evolution

items.title: Promote full LLM-wiki from sleeping future item to a thresholded active roadmap
items.summary: Full LLM-wiki has explicit activation criteria, owner gates, non-goals, and a first implementation tranche that does not prematurely enable heavy RAG.

items.title: Enforce retrieval observation metrics for FTS, RAG, and GraphRAG escalation
items.summary: Real retrieval misses and noisy lookup events are recorded in a structured place and checked before route escalation.

items.title: Define version coupling between RedCap runtime and external redcap-arsenal
items.summary: RedCap records which arsenal commit/head was validated and how runtime releases reference compatible arsenal states.

items.title: Consolidate root-level information architecture before product release
items.summary: Produce a Prism-reviewed root-level information architecture consolidation plan that inventories every root-level asset root, classifies it, defines a target parent model, maps aliases and consumers, and only then opens

items.title: Apply root-level information architecture physical consolidation through safe semantic tranches
items.summary: Closed for the current pre-release pass by completing the shared-knowledge template physical tranche and explicitly deferring high-risk root groups before release readiness.

items.title: Run a senior holistic RedCap architecture smell audit instead of closing user examples one by one
items.summary: Produce a Prism-reviewed senior holistic architecture smell audit that explicitly reviews multiple domains, records 'found / not found / deferred' conclusions per domain, and gives every finding a durable disposition ins

groups.title: Holistic audit follow-up before release readiness

items.title: Make human-facing CLI, status, and notification output understandable without RedCap internal jargon
items.summary: Human-facing output is framed by problem, action, result, current task panorama, next step, and whether human intervention is needed. Internal mechanism names may appear only as secondary evidence links or glossary-backe

items.title: Separate public runtime contract from maintainer-only governance validators before npm or CLI release
items.summary: Release readiness distinguishes the public runtime contract from maintainer/developer governance tools. The package manifest, runtime package readiness policy, and publish safety check agree on that boundary from a singl

items.title: Track Prism degradation frequency and keep conclusion gates resilient when providers are flaky
items.summary: Prism status surfaces show the recent degradation rate, provider families involved, and whether the current task used full quorum or resource-limited evidence. Degradation above a defined threshold opens a governance act

groups.title: Plan-only closure and Prism follow-up hardening

items.title: Strengthen Prism and conclusion gates to catch plan-only closure follow-up gaps
items.summary: Prism prompts, conclusion policy, and closeout-facing validators require reviewers to check whether every deferred capability or future apply requirement has a durable task, backlog item, owner surface, or explicit no-fo

execution_order.title: Fast consistency and truth-surface repairs
execution_order.summary: Fix low-cost drift that misleads humans or agents even when runtime checks pass.

execution_order.title: Knowledge architecture foundations
execution_order.summary: Turn the current multi-root knowledge layout into a deliberate federated retrieval system instead of a loose pile of knowledge directories.

execution_order.title: Policy, evidence, and legacy-asset hygiene
execution_order.summary: Reduce policy sprawl, evidence accumulation, and old/new transition ambiguity without damaging archaeology.

execution_order.title: Runtime and host-adapter productization
execution_order.summary: Move from skill-root compatibility to a cleaner installable runtime and host-adapter shape.

execution_order.title: Advanced memory and shared arsenal evolution
execution_order.summary: Keep full LLM-wiki, retrieval escalation, and public arsenal maturity visible without prematurely enabling heavyweight memory systems.

execution_order.title: Root product-shape consolidation
execution_order.summary: Root product-shape consolidation is closed for the current pre-release pass: RASG-017 produced the target model, and RASG-022 completed one safe physical tranche plus explicit deferral of high-risk root groups.

execution_order.title: Senior holistic smell audit
execution_order.summary: Prevent user examples from being narrowed into single-point fixes by requiring a Prism-reviewed, senior-engineering review across RedCap's product shape, workflow guarantees, truth sources, knowledge/evidence lifecycle, package surface, and human-facing status model.

execution_order.title: Holistic audit follow-up before release readiness
execution_order.summary: Track the P1 issues discovered by RASG-018 that should be closed before RedCap is treated as a polished public runtime or CLI product.

execution_order.title: Plan-only closure and Prism follow-up hardening
execution_order.summary: Prevent design-only, plan-only, or route-only work from being treated as fully closed when a later physical apply or governance hardening task was explicitly required.
